images.text:
Candice: It's so great to meet you in person, Amy. Vanessa speaks very highly of you.
Amy: Thanks, she is a great student and friend.
Candice: So, I understand you're interested in potentially getting involved?
Amy: Exactly, I've been very fortunate in my life, and I feel like I absolutely must give something back.
Candice: Great. Let me tell you a little bit about what we do. We are committed to ending the AIDS pandemic in Lesotho and doing all we can for the 200,000 orphans who live there.
Amy: My god, it sounds awful.

Candice: It is. And we must do something about it. To start, we had a local company recruit a project manager. His name is Samuel, and he is from Maseru, the capital.
Amy: It's great that you're making use of local expertise. A lot of non-governmental organizations failed to do this in the past.
Candice: Exactly, we really had to rethink things. Newton has been such a huge help. He had experts brought in to spearhead education initiatives. Then, he had a few foster homes built.

Amy: This all sounds so ambitious. I'm really not sure if I am suited for it. How would I fit in?
Candice: Well, you have to get some first-hand experience, to see if you're up to the challenge.
Amy: I don't think I'm ready to ship out to Africa just yet.
Candice: That's not what I mean. You don't have to go abroad to get experience. why don't you try something local? I know a guy who runs a local soup kitchen. I'll have him give you some volunteer work this Sunday. If you make it through that, then we'll set you up with some projects here.
Amy: Sounds great!

These are words you use to talk about doing charity work.
to give time or service to your community
Example: I feel like I absolutely must give something back.
a child whose parents have passed away
Example: We are committed to ending the AIDS pandemic in Lesotho and doing all we can for the 200, 000 orphans who live there.
a social organization that is not connected to a government agency
Example: A lot of non-governmental organizations failed to help in the past.
to think again about how something is done
Example: We really had to rethink things.
Example: He had experts brought in to spearhead education initiatives.
Example: Well, you have to get some first-hand experience, to see if you're up to the challenge.
Example: You don't have to go abroad to get experience.
Example: The education initiative has been a huge success.
You use the causative verb to have to refer to a situation when someone does, did, or will do something for another person.
There are two structures you can use with the causative verb to have:

1. To have something done
To have + object + past participle

For example:
He had a few foster homes built.

1. To have someone do something
To have + person + verb

For example:
I'll have him give you some volunteer work this Sunday.
He had experts brought in to spearhead education initiatives.
We had a local company recruit a project manager.
Expressing Necessity: Must/Have to/Have got to
You use the modal verbs and phrases must, have to and have got to to express necessity in the past and present.
Must refers to obligations which come from the speaker and may be directed at the speaker (when talking about personal goals) or the listener (when talking about obligations):

I really must give up smoking. (directed at the speaker)
You must keep this secret. (directed at the listener)
Must has no past form. You use had to to express past obligations:
When I was in school, I had to play a lot of sports.
Have to expresses external obligations, which come from outside of the speaker. These may be rules and regulations imposed by an external authority:

I have to get to work by 9 every day.
Do you have to do any community service?
The past tense of have to is had to.

You use don't have to (not mustn't) to express an absence of obligation.
Mustn't is used to express that it is necessary not to do something:

I don't have to get up early tomorrow. It's Sunday. (I can get up late.)
You mustn't tell anyone. It's a secret. (Don't tell anyone.)
I absolutely must give something back.
You have to get some first-hand experience.
You don't have to go abroad to get experience.
We really had to rethink things.
